questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about where you are going.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually provides good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except when it is raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: When positioning your body on the motorcycle:

options.text: Hold yourself up with your arms.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms do the steering, not the holding up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when you hold the handgrips.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in ______ of a lane.
questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: When shifting gears in a curve:

options.text: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
It is better than shifting before the curve.
It is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before turning. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can cause a skid.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going and how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of large vehicles can judge your speed and location correctly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
Have no wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: If you need to react to a hazard in the road, do not:

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers where you are.
Use your horn and/or lights or signals to let others know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers where you are.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers where you are by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed and lane position as needed to stay safe.

questions.question: When riding, you should check your mirrors:

options.text: Constantly by staring in the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regularly and often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while riding. Always use your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When you and another vehicle reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Press your knees against the gas tank.
Keep your arms straight when holding the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should be slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank to help you balance.

questions.question: An engine seizes because of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not enough oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when they run low on oil. Without oil, the engine's parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level. Turning your shoulders can cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:
questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Leave more space when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase your distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them visible.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross quickly.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. Slow down at intersections. Avoid changing speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, press the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: Helmets are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-compliant helmet every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it alone to stay safe.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together. Also downshift as you stop.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean your body toward the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean your body toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Always lean your body in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to steering changes:
questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle. The extra weight causes the motorcycle to respond more slowly to steering, speeding up, slowing down, and turning.

questions.question: Motorcycles are most likely to have conflicts with other traffic:
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful when approaching intersections.
